status: Engineering inventory; privacy owner must approve store answers and retention before beta.

data.retention: Provider cleanup and backup periods require approval
Logout clears local values; iOS uninstall can retain Keychain entries

fields: workspace ID scoped by environment and user
data.retention: Cleared on account or environment changes

data.purpose: Read work and send explicit messages
data.location: Process memory; Talyn backend and configured providers
data.retention: No new persistent content cache; backend retention requires approval

fields: alert text: session names, agent summaries, questions and errors, PR references and titles
data.purpose: Optional alerts with desktop-style text (Tom's call, 2026-11-12) and authorized tap resolution. Expo, FCM, and APNs receive the alert text; the data payload holds only opaque IDs
data.location: SecureStore installation ID; encrypted backend token; Expo Push Service; APNs; FCM
data.retention: See docs/MOBILE_PUSH_NOTIFICATIONS.md; approve processors before activation
Infrastructure logging and provider policies require review. App analytics is listed separately under PostHog.

fields: persistent EAS client ID sent as EAS-Client-ID
data.purpose: Compatible software delivery over HTTPS from EAS. Updates are unsigned by decision (2026-11-09). Enabled in preview, internal-beta, and production builds; the development client loads from Metro and sends no update requests
data.location: Expo EAS Update; device update cache; native UserDefaults or SharedPreferences for the EAS client ID
data.retention: The EAS client ID and update cache can survive logout. The privacy owner must review Expo retention, uninstall, backup, and native cache behavior before beta.

fields: images the person picks from the photo library
photos the person takes with the camera
data.purpose: Attach images to a chat message or to the first message of a new session, only when the person chooses to
data.location: System photo picker and camera (permission asked on first use); uploaded to the session sandbox through the Talyn backend. For a new session, made smaller on the phone and sent inline with the first message
data.retention: Kept with the session's sandbox files. A new session's queued first message holds them until its turn starts; backend and sandbox retention require approval

fields: clipboard text when it looks like a Claude sign-in code
data.purpose: Prefill the Claude sign-in code field; the person confirms before it is sent
data.location: Process memory only; sent to the Talyn backend only when the person submits

fields: Anthropic or OpenAI API keys the person enters
data.location: Sent once to the Talyn backend, which keeps them encrypted; not stored on the device
data.retention: Until the person removes the account or deletes the workspace

fields: last repository used to start a session, by workspace or space
data.purpose: Restore the person's choices on this device
data.location: AsyncStorage, scoped by environment and user where it names account data
data.retention: Onboarding progress and space choice clear on sign-out; theme, the analytics choice and the last repository stay until changed or the app is removed

data.purpose: Show the plan and let the person upgrade or buy credits
data.location: Talyn backend; checkout and portal run on Polar in the browser, not in the app
data.retention: Polar is the merchant of record; its retention and Talyn's billing records require approval

data.category: Product analytics, session replay, and diagnostics
fields: Supabase user ID as the distinct ID, with email and GitHub username as person properties
anonymous PostHog device ID before sign-in
usage events with IDs and settings, never titles, prompts, transcripts, code, or repository names
screen names as route patterns with no IDs
touch autocapture by component name and test ID
masked session replay: text, inputs, images, and sandboxed views are masked; no console logs or network requests
exceptions with stack traces, the online state, and a connectivity flag
native crash reports (iOS, Android JVM, and Android NDK) with native stack traces, sent on the next launch for an NDK crash
device and app info: platform, OS, model, locale, timezone, app version and build, OTA update ID and channel, release environment
app lifecycle events (installed, updated, opened, backgrounded)
IP address as seen by PostHog ingestion
data.purpose: First-party product analytics, session replay of the app UI, and crash and error diagnostics. Tom reversed the MVP rule of no analytics or replay on 2026-11-10
data.location: PostHog (project from EXPO_PUBLIC_TALYN_POSTHOG_KEY, US ingestion by default); SDK queue and anonymous ID in the app document directory
data.retention: PostHog project retention. Settings > Account > "Share usage data and session replays" turns it off on the device from the next event, and stops replay. No key in the build means nothing is sent. Replay is off in development builds

processors: Expo Push Service and EAS Update
Configured coding-agent and repository providers through the existing backend
Polar checkout and customer portal, opened in the browser
Anthropic Claude sign-in, opened in the browser
GitHub App installation, opened in the browser
PostHog product analytics, session replay, and error tracking (first-party use, no cross-app tracking)

applePreparation.collectedDataTypes: Do not infer a no-collection answer from the app manifest. Declare Product Interaction, Crash Data, Other Diagnostic Data, and the User ID (linked to the person, not used for tracking) for PostHog, plus linked account data and content. Review processor practices.
applePreparation.requiredReasonApis: Inspect merged archive manifests from React Native, Expo, AsyncStorage, SecureStore, and updates. Approve reasons from actual use. Do not copy generic reason codes.

googlePreparation.collection: Review account data, messages, app activity (PostHog usage events and session replay), identifiers (user ID), and diagnostics (crash logs) against current Console definitions.
googlePreparation.sharing: Assess processors and service-provider exceptions with the privacy owner.
googlePreparation.security: Verify HTTPS transport and deletion completion. Do not attest to full deletion or encryption scope without evidence.
googlePreparation.deletion: In-app deletion exists. Publish an unauthenticated deletion page with paying-admin restrictions and partial-cleanup support.
